messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] failover-monitor: region-health-us-west1 crossed degradation threshold (error_rate 4.7%, latency_p95 980ms) — auto-failover candidate. link: https://console.redwood/integrations/dashboards/region-health
oncall-maya: picking this up — getting page. checking routing table + LB metrics now.
mike: FYI customers with endpoints in us-west1 may see increased latency or 502s. CS notified. cc @cs-alex
oncall-maya: seeing surge of 5xx from inference gateway: nginx upstream timeout spikes, connections reset. k8s pod restarts in node pool a, node network flapping logs around the same time.
lucy: putting ingress in debug for a minute, dumping top error logs. also enabling prefix-caching bypass for critical routes.
oncall-maya: running quick mitigation: draining ngw-us-west1-3 and shifting traffic to us-west2 and eu-west1 via smart-router override.

sre-lead: good. coordinate with routing policy: set smart-router weight us-west1=0.15, us-west2=0.6, eu-west1=0.25. keep canary window open 5m.

oncall-maya: applied weights via runtime-control. Command:
```
rtctl set-weights --policy smart-router --region-weights us-west1:15,us-west2:60,eu-west1:25
```
oncall-maya: watching cross-region latency and token throughput. initial fallbacks look healthy, error rate down to 0.9% in 4m.

ta o: noted that failover-monitor produced several duplicate alerts during the flapping — we need to suppress repeated triggers while mitigating.

mike: CS update: three enterprise customers reported elevated latency for 4–12 minutes, no request drops reported; we pushed brief status note. #customers asked for root cause if we have it yet.

lucy: root cause appears to be intermittent network interface errors on two hosts in the us-west1 node pool after a host-level kernel update rolled out yesterday. Network team investigating.

sre-lead: mitigation checklist
- maintain weight shift until node repairs complete
- keep prefix caching bypass for critical endpoints
- increase autoscaler min to avoid pods terminating on flappy nodes
- reduce alert noise by suppressing identical failover-monitor alerts for 10m

oncall-maya: raising a short-lived pager suppression rule for failover-monitor in us-west1 to reduce noise and avoid repeated escalation while we stabilize.

mike: CS will send a follow-up to impacted customers summarizing what we know and mitigation in progress. tagging legal for enterprise customers with strict SLAs.

incident-bot: suppression rule created by oncall-maya: failover-monitor(us-west1) -> silence 10m (auto-unmute)

oncall-maya: after 25m of monitoring, error rate stable ~0.6%, latency back to baseline in most routes. keeping an eye for 30m before fully relaxing weight shift.

ta o: post-incident action items (PIA) suggestions:
- tune failover-monitor alert: change from alerting on raw error_rate>3% to a rolling 5m avg + require sustained increase for 3m
- add a secondary check for cross-region traffic-shift to detect sudden weight changes >10% in 1m
- create a dedicated multi-region health dashboard showing traffic weights, 95th latency per region, and per-route KV cache hitrate
- add alert dedupe/suppression in incident-bot for flapping conditions

sre-lead: +1 to all. I'll own the alert rule change and dashboard. Assigning tasks now:
- sre-lead: update failover-monitor alert rule and add dedupe logic (ETA EOD)
- lucy: coordinate with infra team for kernel rollback/patch validation (ETA 2h)
- tao: add automated dashboard panels and a failover alert that fires if routing weight changes >15% in 1m (ETA tomorrow morning)
- oncall-maya: create runbook snippet for regional drain + smart-router weight override (ETA tonight)
- mike: produce postmortem and customer impact spreadsheet (ETA 24h)

cs-alex: leaving note for enterprise recipients: we will include timeline, impact, and mitigations. please flag any customers who need more immediate high-touch follow-up.

sre-lead: quick draft for alert rule change (Prometheus-style pseudo):
```
ALERT RegionFailing
IF increase(region_error_rate{region="us-west1"}[5m]) > 2 and avg_over_time(region_error_rate{region="us-west1"}[5m]) > 0.03
FOR 3m
LABELS {severity="page"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary="Sustained increased error rate in us-west1"}
```
This adds a sustained window and a rate-of-change clause to avoid flapping noise.

tao: for the dashboard I'll surface a function that correlates weight shifts with 95th latency. sample query:
- weight_change = rate(smart_router_weight_change_total[1m])
- latency_p95 by region
then panel: if weight_change>0.15 && latency_p95>800ms -> trigger advisory.

oncall-maya: handoff to night oncall @tao in 30m. leaving context:
- mitigation in place: weights adjusted, suppression enabled, prefix cache bypass active
- root cause probable: kernel update + NIC instability on nodes us-west1
- current status: error rate ~0.6%, latency near baseline, continue monitoring for 2h.

tao: acknowledged. will monitor and escalate if any sign of regression. I'll implement the dashboard panels in the next runbook cycle.

sre-lead: thanks everyone. addendum: we should also add a synthetic probe that runs cross-region failover exercises hourly in staging to surface these kinds of routing surprises before production.

mike: logging action item: enable a short-lived log sink for the 12m window where most 502s occurred so we can capture full traces for customers who request them.

incident-bot: incident resolved for region us-west1: state=stabilized, duration=47m. Post-incident review scheduled in #postmortems in 48h.

oncall-maya: closing the loop here — leaving any remaining notes in the incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1738456789

cs-alex: will follow up with customers in the morning. thanks all. :thumbsup:
